1: use ruff_diagnostics::{Diagnostic, Edit, Fix, FixAvailability, Violation};
2: use ruff_macros::{derive_message_formats, ViolationMetadata};
3: use ruff_python_trivia::CommentRanges;
4: use ruff_source_file::{LineRanges, UniversalNewlineIterator};
5: use ruff_text_size::TextRange;
6: 
7: use crate::settings::LinterSettings;
8: use crate::Locator;
9: 
10: use super::super::detection::comment_contains_code;
11: 
12: /// ## What it does
13: /// Checks for commented-out Python code.
14: ///
15: /// ## Why is this bad?
16: /// Commented-out code is dead code, and is often included inadvertently.
17: /// It should be removed.
18: ///
19: /// ## Known problems
20: /// Prone to false positives when checking comments that resemble Python code,
21: /// but are not actually Python code ([#4845]).
22: ///
23: /// ## Example
24: /// ```python
25: /// # print("Hello, world!")
26: /// ```
27: ///
28: /// ## Options
29: /// - `lint.task-tags`
30: ///
31: /// [#4845]: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff/issues/4845
32: #[derive(ViolationMetadata)]
33: pub(crate) struct CommentedOutCode;
34: 
35: impl Violation for CommentedOutCode {
36:     const FIX_AVAILABILITY: FixAvailability = FixAvailability::None;
37: 
38:     #[derive_message_formats]
39:     fn message(&self) -> String {
40:         "Found commented-out code".to_string()
41:     }
42: 
43:     fn fix_title(&self) -> Option<String> {
44:         Some("Remove commented-out code".to_string())
45:     }
46: }
47: 
48: /// ERA001
49: pub(crate) fn commented_out_code(
50:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
51:     locator: &Locator,
52:     comment_ranges: &CommentRanges,
53:     settings: &LinterSettings,
54: ) {
55:     let mut comments = comment_ranges.into_iter().peekable();
56:     // Iterate over all comments in the document.
57:     while let Some(range) = comments.next() {
58:         let line = locator.line_str(range.start());
59: 
60:         if is_script_tag_start(line) {
61:             if skip_script_comments(range, &mut comments, locator) {
62:                 continue;
63:             }
64:         }
65: 
66:         // Verify that the comment is on its own line, and that it contains code.
67:         if is_own_line_comment(line) && comment_contains_code(line, &settings.task_tags[..]) {
68:             let mut diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(CommentedOutCode, range);
69:             diagnostic.set_fix(Fix::display_only_edit(Edit::range_deletion(
70:                 locator.full_lines_range(range),
71:             )));
72:             diagnostics.push(diagnostic);
73:         }
74:     }
75: }
76: 
77: /// Parses the rest of a [PEP 723](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/)
78: /// script comment and moves `comments` past the script comment's end unless
79: /// the script comment is invalid.
80: ///
81: /// Returns `true` if it is a valid script comment.
82: fn skip_script_comments<I>(
83:     script_start: TextRange,
84:     comments: &mut std::iter::Peekable<I>,
85:     locator: &Locator,
86: ) -> bool
87: where
88:     I: Iterator<Item = TextRange>,
89: {
90:     let line_end = locator.full_line_end(script_start.end());
91:     let rest = locator.after(line_end);
92:     let mut end_offset = None;
93:     let mut lines = UniversalNewlineIterator::with_offset(rest, line_end);
94: 
95:     while let Some(line) = lines.next() {
96:         let Some(content) = script_line_content(&line) else {
97:             break;
98:         };
99: 
100:         if content == "///" {
101:             // > Precedence for an ending line # /// is given when the next line is not a valid
102:             // > embedded content line as described above.
103:             // > For example, the following is a single fully valid block:
104:             // > ```python
105:             // > # /// some-toml
106:             // > # embedded-csharp = """
107:             // > # /// <summary>
108:             // > # /// text
109:             // > # ///
110:             // > # /// </summary>
111:             // > # public class MyClass { }
112:             // > # """
113:             // > # ///
114:             // ````
115:             if lines.next().is_some_and(|line| is_valid_script_line(&line)) {
116:                 continue;
117:             }
118:             end_offset = Some(line.full_end());
119:             break;
120:         }
121:     }
122: 
123:     // > Unclosed blocks MUST be ignored.
124:     let Some(end_offset) = end_offset else {
125:         return false;
126:     };
127: 
128:     // Skip over all script-comments.
129:     while let Some(comment) = comments.peek() {
130:         if comment.start() >= end_offset {
131:             break;
132:         }
133: 
134:         comments.next();
135:     }
136: 
137:     true
138: }
139: 
140: fn script_line_content(line: &str) -> Option<&str> {
141:     let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix('#') else {
142:         // Not a comment
143:         return None;
144:     };
145: 
146:     // An empty line
147:     if rest.is_empty() {
148:         return Some("");
149:     }
150: 
151:     // > If there are characters after the # then the first character MUST be a space.
152:     rest.strip_prefix(' ')
153: }
154: 
155: fn is_valid_script_line(line: &str) -> bool {
156:     script_line_content(line).is_some()
157: }
158: 
159: /// Returns `true` if line contains an own-line comment.
160: fn is_own_line_comment(line: &str) -> bool {
161:     for char in line.chars() {
162:         if char == '#' {
163:             return true;
164:         }
165:         if !char.is_whitespace() {
166:             return false;
167:         }
168:     }
169:     unreachable!("Comment should contain '#' character")
170: }
171: 
172: /// Returns `true` if the line appears to start a script tag.
173: ///
174: /// See: <https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/>
175: fn is_script_tag_start(line: &str) -> bool {
176:     line == "# /// script"
177: }

part.text: The ERA001 rule is in `crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/eradicate/rules/commented_out_code.rs`. The bug: `skip_script_comments` consumes the next line after `# ///` via `lines.next()`, so when `# ///` is followed by more comment lines (like `#` or `# Bla bla bla`, which are valid "script lines"), it never registers the block end, and the whole block gets re-scanned as regular comments. part.text:
Fixed. The change is in `skip_script_comments` (crates/ruff_linter/src/rules/eradicate/rules/commented_out_code.rs:95):

- **Root cause**: When a `# ///` closing line was followed by more comment lines (e.g. `#`, `# Bla bla bla`), the old "precedence" lookahead consumed the next line, saw a valid script line, and kept scanning — so the block never closed, `skip_script_comments` returned `false`, and the metadata block was re-scanned as ordinary comments, flagging `# dependencies = [` and `# ]` as ERA001.
- **Fix**: The script block now ends at the last `# ///` content line (set `end_offset` on every `///` and keep scanning until a non-script line), removing the lookahead and `is_valid_script_line`. Comments before that offset are skipped; trailing normal comments are then checked as usual.

Validation:
- All 13 `eradicate` unit tests pass, including the updated snapshot test (`ERA001.py` fixture with the "script block followed by normal block" case) and the `script_comment_end_precedence` test.
- The exact reproduction from the issue passes (`cargo run -p ruff -- check --select ERA001` → "All checks passed!").
